You will have a balance between a tactical and strategic approach to issues and solutions within the disciplines of planning, scheduling, and overall materials processes within the site. This position offers a 1st shift, on-site schedule at our East Aurora, NY Location. To be considered for the Operations Planning Manager role, here’s what you’ll typically need to bring with you: Bachelor’s degree in a Technical or Business discipline, with 5+ years of relevant experience. 2+ years of leadership experience, including demonstrated capability of: Leading, developing and coaching high-performing teams of employees. Leading through influence and partnering with cross-functional teams to develop and deliver tactical plans that achieve operation objectives. Effectively leading through organizational changes. A continuous improvement mindset, with a proven track record of enacting lean manufacturing strategies and implementing process improvements. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Legally authorized to work in the US without company sponsorship. CPIM or APICS certification preferred. As an Operations Planning Manager, you will: Lead the site Hydraulic A&T in developing & deploying a successful material planning strategy based on current load and future growth, with a result of proper inventory management. Develop and implement tools, processes, training aids, and standard work to drive continuous improvement within the Planning/Materials function for Hydraulic A&T. Lead a team of direct reporting Planners demonstrating Moog Culture and Values, and work cross functionally with many areas (e.g. fabrication, engineers, HR, lean, quality, supply chain, etc.). Develop tactical plans to achieve the Hydraulic A&T and Site’s strategic objectives, including being directly responsible for planning processes and settings for all value streams Facilitate resolution of all issues that may impact objectives with a major focus on delivery. Work closely and effectively communicate with your counterparts and Planners in Fabrication and Supply Chain to ensure seamless part supply and quick problem resolution. Coordinate with Demand Management for capacity analysis and review, to highlight work center bottlenecks or constraints and provide staffing and equipment recommendations for Operations. Ensure that relevant, accurate, and timely communication and reports are acquired from and delivered to stakeholders. Have responsibility for on time delivery of piece part customer orders for Hydraulic A&T How We Care for You: Financial Rewards: great compensation package, annual profit sharing, matching 401k, and the ability to participate in Employee Stock Purchase Plan, Flexible Spending and Health Savings Accounts Work/Life Balance: Flexible paid time off, holidays and parental leave program, relocation assistance and occasional ability to work from home. Health & Welfare: Comprehensive insurance coverage including medical, dental, vision, life, disability, Employee Assistance Plan (“EAP”) and other supplemental benefit coverages. Professional Skills Development: Tuition Assistance, mentorship and coaching opportunities, leadership development and other personal growth programs. Collaborative and Welcoming Workplace: Inclusive culture rooted in our values, enhanced by Employee Resource Groups, and team-building activities. Additional site-specific benefits may be offered. Plant Quality Manager — McKenzie, TN Job Summary: We are seeking an experienced Quality Manager to lead product quality and reliability for a metal fabrication plant producing steel doors and frames for high‑end rated applications. This plant leadership role combines management responsibilities with hands‑on Quality Engineer activities: active shop‑floor engagement, rapid issue containment, disciplined root‑cause analysis and verification. The role is a member of the plant leadership team, reports to the Plant Manager, and will work closely with the operations team and Product Management to prioritize projects, resolve production issues, and improve operational performance. Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to be employed in the United States. The company does not intend to provide sponsorship for employment visa status (e.g., H-1B, TN, etc.) for this employment position. Key Responsibilities: Develop, implement and sustain the plant Quality system and procedures tailored to rated steel doors and frames. Maintain a regular visible presence on the shop floor (Gemba), actively engaging with operators and supervisors to identify and resolve quality issues in real time. Partner closely with production and operations leadership to prevent and resolve production quality issues and to integrate quality requirements into daily operations. Lead containment and corrective actions for non‑conforming material; implement, verify and close CAPA. Drive root‑cause analysis using structured tools (8D, 5 Whys, fishbone, PFMEA, A3) and ensure robust verification and prevention plans. Provide SPC support and training; implement control charts and process capability monitoring for critical fabrication, welding and finishing processes. Oversee receiving inspection, in‑process and final inspections, first‑article inspections/FAI, gage calibration and MSA (including gage R&R). Support weld inspection, dimensional tolerance control, hardware preparation, coatings/finishing inspection and other critical checks specific to rated product production. Develop and maintain control plans, inspection criteria and process validations required for rated applications and customer specifications. Manage supplier quality for purchased components (hinges, hardware, gasketing, glazing), including incoming inspection and supplier corrective actions. Lead quality projects to documented completion, track metrics and report status to Plant Manager and leadership. Drive continuous improvement and lean initiatives to eliminate waste, increase throughput and maintain product integrity; apply structured change management to sustain improvements. Manage internal quality audits and ensure compliance with applicable standards for rated products. Act as customer/supplier liaison on quality matters; support field issues, claims or investigations when required. Coach, develop and lead the quality team; deliver hands‑on training and mentoring to production personnel. Required Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or related field, or equivalent experience. Minimum 5 years’ experience in a manufacturing environment leading quality or engineering functions with demonstrated hands‑on shop‑floor experience. Direct experience in metal fabrication preferred; experience with steel doors, frames, or similar rated metal products strongly preferred. Practical knowledge of root‑cause analysis, SPC, MSA (gage R&R), PFMEA, control plans and CAPA systems. Job Summary Position Summary: We are seeking a Production Engineer to support operations at our water chemical treatment facility across two key areas: Production and Logistics. This role requires a hands-on engineering professional who will optimize processes, ensure safety compliance, and drive continuous improvement initiatives while managing both production operations and supply chain logistics. Key Characteristics: Strong Analytical and Problem-Solving Skills - The role requires conducting root cause analysis, investigating quality concerns and equipment non-conformances, performing supply chain optimization analysis, and continuously making decisions to improve process efficiencies. The engineer must be able to systematically identify issues, analyze complex data (like OEE metrics), and develop effective countermeasures. Excellent Communication and Training Abilities - The position involves networking with site, regional, and global functions, performing classroom instruction for operations teams, coordinating with vendors, and managing cross-functional relationships between production and logistics. The engineer must effectively communicate technical concepts to diverse audiences and facilitate knowledge transfer. Strong Organizational and Project Management Skills - The role requires balancing multiple responsibilities across two locations (Production and Logistics), managing over 36 bulk storage tanks, coordinating scheduling for materials/packaging/shipments, identifying and executing CAPEX/OPEX projects, and maintaining documentation. The engineer must prioritize tasks effectively, manage timelines, and ensure compliance across various operational areas simultaneously. Duties & Responsibilities Support all Environmental, Health, and Safety programs, policies, and regulations Coordinate Management of Change (MOC) and Process Safety Management (PSM) operational opportunities Perform process engineering activities including heat/material transfer, mass balancing, and equipment performance assessments Conduct root cause analysis and implement appropriate countermeasures for operational issues Network with site, regional, and global functions to drive best practices Production Focus Areas: Manage bulk storage, production equipment, auxiliary systems, and utilities Track and analyze Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) data to identify quality concerns, yield losses, and equipment non-conformances Monitor daily production and quality rates to ensure optimal performance Identify, scope, and execute CAPEX and OPEX improvement projects Provide training and classroom instruction to operations teams Support production scheduling and maintain critical documentation Logistics Focus Areas: Balance daily administrative duties (25-40% of time) with field support activities Coordinate raw material scheduling and ensure adequate storage space availability Manage packaging schedules and prepare required documentation Oversee shipment scheduling and documentation preparation Conduct vendor management and maintain chemical organization per segregation/lean standards Perform supply chain analysis for optimization opportunities Manage over 36 bulk storage tanks and develop equipment handling procedures Conduct inventory accuracy assessments and ensure risk management compliance This dual-role position offers the opportunity to gain comprehensive understanding of both production operations and logistics management while driving process improvements and maintaining the highest safety and quality standards in water chemical treatment operations.
